DEC-044.title: ISS-064: keep sequence-packing config as documented-deferral (neither wire nor remove)
DEC-044.rationale: Both candidate actions are worse than the status quo. (a) Wiring SequencePacker::pack_sequences into compose_prefill_with_packing changes batch composition by similarity/limit-reordering: it reorders/merges sequences before prefill, which would interact with the ISS-051 chunked-prefill path, the hardened ISS-052/055/056 preemption + decode-growth paths, and prefill admission ordering (shorter-first sort) — high regression risk for an optimization whose measured benefit is unproven. (b) Removing the inert gate deletes a complete designed feature surface (SequencePackingConfig + from_env + builder + SchedulerConfig.packing + BatchComposer::with_packing + SequencePacker in scheduler/packing.rs) that represents a plausible future optimization; unlike PreemptionManager (misleading 'planned' doc + conflicting policy), prefill.rs explicitly documents the deferral and no CLI flag exposes it. Decision: leave the config plumbed but inert, with the existing explicit deferral documentation; re-evaluate if/when a measured throughput gap justifies the wiring risk. Contrasts with ISS-063 where removal (not deferral) was correct because the dead policy conflicted with the verified path and misled.
DEC-044.alternatives_rejected: (a) wire pack_sequences into compose_prefill_with_packing [rejected: regresses ISS-051/052/055/056 paths, unproven benefit]; (b) remove inert gate + config surface [rejected: destroys designed feature, honest doc already exists]
